rendered_html: 📔 Regulatory Bulletin — 18 November 2026 (Daily) Executive Summary • 🟡 The SFC has updated its DPRK-sanctions circular for licensed corporations, SFC-licensed virtual-asset service providers and associated entities; in-scope firms should confirm the amended entity record is reflected in sanctions screening. • 🟡 HKIMR has published new research on GenAI and agentic-AI adoption in Hong Kong financial services, signalling governance, explainability and security considerations rather than a new regulatory requirement. Hong Kong 🟡 Circular on DPRK sanctions-list update 🇭🇰 Item ID: item-20261117-sfc-aml-circulars-096cf0355a ⏰ Deadline: As soon as practicable whenever there are updates Products: Investment services; virtual-asset services The Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) says the UN Security Council DPRK Sanctions Committee amended an entity record on 13 November 2026 (New York time), and that an updated Hong Kong list under section 31 of Cap. 537AE was published on 17 November. The circular is addressed to licensed corporations, SFC-licensed virtual-asset service providers and their associated entities, and the SFC expects them to screen all new or revised designations against client lists as soon as practicable whenever there are updates, under its AML/CFT Guideline. This is a sanctions-data update rather than a new sanctions regime; direct applicability to an authorised institution outside the stated SFC population is not established by the circular. In-scope operations may need to verify data-feed deployment, alert handling and retained screening evidence for the amended record. Source: Circular to Licensed Corporations, SFC-licensed Virtual Asset Service Providers and Associated Entities — Anti-Money Laundering / Counter-Financing of Terrorism: United Nations Sanctions (Democratic People’s Republic of Korea) Regulation 🟡 Research report on AI adoption, governance and compliance 🇭🇰 Item ID: item-20261117-hkma-press-1b20b9fb3f ⏰ Deadline: No source deadline stated Products: Digital services The Hong Kong Institute for Monetary and Financial Research (HKIMR), the Hong Kong Academy of Finance’s research arm, released research on GenAI and agentic-AI adoption in Hong Kong financial services. The report draws on a January–July 2026 survey and interviews; it reports 90% current or planned GenAI adoption and identifies explainability and security as adoption challenges. It is research and market intelligence, not an HKMA rule, supervisory expectation or finding of deficient controls. It signals that digital and compliance teams may need to assess whether AI use cases have appropriate governance, security, explainability, data and third-party oversight before material deployment. Source: Report on “From Assistance to Autonomy: A.I. Adoption, Governance, and Compliance in Hong Kong’s Financial Services Industry” Mainland/GBA • No validated Mainland/GBA items in this run.
